comments.text: From facet_pi security audit Finding 2 (Medium): conversations.ex:386 @allowed_update_keys includes 'messages' => :messages, letting a client replace the entire message array, bypassing schema validation and ContextSanitizer. This is an authorization/logic gap — Catseye can't detect this via taint analysis. Possible detection: code smell rule that flags maps named 'allowed_keys' or 'permitted_fields' that include sensitive field names like 'messages', 'password', 'role', 'permissions', 'admin'. This is a low-confidence heuristic but catches a common API design mistake.

title: Elixir: detect dangerous keys in allowed-update/whitelist maps (messages, password, permissions)
